title.en: Western Jin: reunification and renewed fragmentation

summary.en:
The Western Jin belongs on the timeline before the end of the Three Kingdoms, not only after it. Its ruling house replaced Wei while Wu still survived in the south. A brief reunification therefore sits within a longer dynastic span, followed by renewed political fragmentation. Reading overlapping bars makes that distinction visible.

Material culture also complicates a history told only through conquests. A Western Jin funerary urn in the Metropolitan Museum combines a model palace, auspicious animals and Buddhist figures. The museum interprets this as evidence of Buddhism entering existing beliefs about the afterlife. The object cannot establish an imperial frontier, but it opens another question: what changed in religious life while political institutions were being remade?
summary.zh:
西晋并非到三国结束后才出现：司马氏取代魏时，南方的吴仍然存在。因此，短暂统一只是较长王朝时段中的一个阶段，随后又出现政治分裂。把同时期政权并排显示，能避免把“建立王朝”和“完成统一”混为一谈。

实物也使这段历史不止于征服。大都会博物馆的一件西晋魂瓶把楼阁、瑞兽与佛像组合在一起，馆方将其解释为佛教逐渐进入本土来世信仰的证据。器物不能证明帝国边界，却能帮助理解：政治制度变化之际，宗教生活也在改变。

dateNote.en: Uses the museum chronology convention 265–316. The Jiangshan source display window begins at 280, after reunification; that is a narrower map-organizing window, not the founding date of Western Jin. Dates are whole-year markers, not day-level succession.
dateNote.zh: 采用博物馆年表的265—316年。江山原项目为组织地图，把西晋显示窗口从统一后的280年开始；这不是西晋建国年。年份为年度尺度，不表示同日完成的政权交接。

en: A dynasty can begin before it controls the territory later associated with it.
Archaeological evidence of religious exchange does not establish political control.
zh: 王朝建立与完成统一并非同一时刻。
宗教交流的考古证据不能直接证明政治控制。

title.en: Eastern Jin: a court in the lower Yangzi

location.label: Jiankang, present-day Nanjing; representative capital location

summary.en:
The Eastern Jin maintained an imperial court in the lower Yangzi while northern China contained competing states. It should appear alongside those northern histories rather than filling a single China-wide succession slot. Jiankang anchors the entry geographically; its location does not imply that the court governed the whole area shown by any broad cultural label.

The southern court was also part of the landscape in which calligraphy, painting and ceramic traditions developed. A fourth-century green-glazed jar catalogued by the Metropolitan Museum provides one dated material example. Political division did not stop cultural production or exchange. Compare this entry with Northern Wei and the later Liu Song to follow both overlapping institutions and changes at the southern court.
summary.zh:
东晋以长江下游为朝廷中心，而北方有多个政权并存。它应当与北方历史并排呈现，而非占据一个代表全中国的单线朝代位置。建康只是本条目的地理锚点，不意味着朝廷统治了所有被文化标签涵盖的地区。

南方也是书法、绘画与陶瓷传统发展的环境。大都会博物馆收藏的一件四世纪青釉四系罐，提供了有年代范围的实物例证。政治分裂并没有使文化生产与交流停止。可把东晋与北魏、后来的刘宋比较，观察同时存在的制度与南方朝廷的更替。

dateNote.en: 317–420 is the museum dynastic interval. Jiankang is representative; the map point is not an extent of rule or a record of uninterrupted peace. The source’s Eastern Jin map phases also include northern contemporaries.
dateNote.zh: 317—420年为博物馆采用的王朝时段。建康点位不代表疆域，也不说明整个时期没有战争。原项目东晋阶段中的地图同时包括北方并存政权。

en: Southern and northern political histories overlap in time.
The southern Jin court continued until the Liu Song succession in 420.
zh: 南北不同政权的历史在时间上重叠。
南方晋廷延续到420年的刘宋更替。

title.en: Northern Wei: state building and Buddhist landscapes
title.zh: 北魏：国家建设与佛教景观

location.label: Pingcheng, present-day Datong; representative early capital

summary.en:
Northern Wei emerged among the competing regimes of northern China and belongs alongside Eastern Jin and the southern dynasties. Its Tuoba Xianbei rulers made Buddhism an important part of the political and artistic landscape. At Yungang near Datong, large cave sanctuaries and sculptural programs make state-supported religious work visible in stone.

The kingdom’s history should not be compressed into a static ethnic label. The source literature describes interaction across northern and southern societies and with Central Asian Buddhist traditions. Nor is a religious site an outline of governmental reach. The end of Northern Wei led into Eastern and Western Wei rather than an immediate reunification of all China; the paired northern successions remain essential context for the Sui.
summary.zh:
北魏兴起于北方多个政权竞争的环境中，与东晋及南朝同时存在。拓跋鲜卑统治者使佛教成为政治和艺术景观的重要部分。大同附近的云冈石窟，以洞窟与造像留下朝廷支持宗教建设的实物证据。

这段历史不能压缩为不变的族群标签。研究资料也讨论南北社会以及中亚佛教传统之间的互动。宗教遗址更不等于行政势力范围。北魏之后出现东魏与西魏，并非立刻实现全中国统一；这些并立和继承关系，是理解隋朝之前局势的必要背景。

dateNote.en: 386–534 follows the Metropolitan Museum and National Museum of China conventions. Some museum summaries end at 535; this atlas retains the dated source convention rather than presenting a day-level transition. The pin references the early capital near Yungang, not every capital phase.
dateNote.zh: 386—534年采用大都会博物馆及中国国家博物馆的纪年；部分概述以535年为终点。本条保留明确来源的年度口径，不伪装成日级交接。点位为云冈附近早期都城平城，并非覆盖全部都城阶段。

en: Northern Wei coexisted with several southern dynasties.
Yungang supplies evidence of religious patronage, not surveyed frontiers.
zh: 北魏与多个南方王朝先后并存。
云冈提供宗教赞助的证据，而非测绘边界。

title.en: Liu Song: a southern dynasty, not the later Song
title.zh: 刘宋：南朝宋与后来的宋朝不同

location.label: Jiankang, present-day Nanjing; representative southern capital

summary.en:
Liu Song was the southern dynasty that followed Eastern Jin in 420. Its name needs an explicit qualifier: it is separated by centuries from the Northern and Southern Song of the tenth to thirteenth centuries. The two uses of “Song” must not merge in search, on the map or in a dynasty sequence.

Northern Wei existed at the same time in the north. Showing both spans is more informative than presenting a single ruler for all China. The period is part of a wider history of courts based at Jiankang and of cultural connections across political divisions. Follow the southern sequence from Eastern Jin to Liu Song, Southern Qi, Liang and Chen, then compare their dates with northern changes.
summary.zh:
刘宋于420年继承东晋，是南方王朝。“宋”必须加以区分：它与十至十三世纪的北宋、南宋相隔数百年，搜索、地图与朝代序列都不应把两者混合。

北方的北魏与之同时存在。并排显示两个政权，比为全中国安排一个统治者更能解释当时局势。刘宋也属于以建康为中心的南方朝廷历史，以及跨越政治分界的文化联系史。可沿东晋、刘宋、南齐、梁、陈的次序阅读，再与北方变化比较。

dateNote.en: 420–479 is the southern Song interval in the cited museum chronology. “Liu Song” distinguishes it from Song 960–1279. The pin identifies Jiankang, not a claim to uniform control across China.
dateNote.zh: 420—479年为引用年表中的南朝宋时段；使用“刘宋”以区别960—1279年的宋朝。点位为建康，不表示统治全中国。

en: Liu Song (420–479) and the Song beginning in 960 are different dynasties.
The dynasty’s span overlaps Northern Wei.
zh: 刘宋（420—479年）与960年开始的宋朝是不同王朝。
刘宋时段与北魏重叠。

title.en: Southern Qi: one court within a divided world
title.zh: 南齐：分裂时代中的一个朝廷

summary.en:
Southern Qi followed Liu Song at Jiankang and preceded Liang. Its short bar belongs within a longer southern sequence, while Northern Wei continued in the north. This makes it possible to ask what a dynastic replacement changes: a ruling house and court institutions can change without every neighboring society starting over.

“Qi” also needs context. Southern Qi is distinct from the Warring States kingdom of Qi and from the later Northern Qi. The atlas keeps separate dates and places for those names. Read the cited regional chronology alongside individual events to distinguish an era label, an imperial house and the territory that a particular map stage actually depicts.
summary.zh:
南齐在建康继承刘宋，之后又由梁取代。它的短时段属于更长的南方朝廷序列，而北魏仍在北方延续。这能帮助提出一个具体问题：王朝更替改变了统治家族与朝廷制度，却并不意味着周边社会同时重新开始。

“齐”也必须结合时空辨认。南齐既不是战国齐国，也不是后来的北齐。本图集以不同年代与地点区分这些名称。把区域年表与具体事件结合阅读，可以避免混淆时代标签、皇室和某个地图阶段实际呈现的辖境。

dateNote.en: 479–502 follows the museum chronology for Southern Qi in South China. This is a dynastic interval, distinct from a map polygon’s source-stage interval.
dateNote.zh: 479—502年采用博物馆所列南齐时段。王朝时段与地图轮廓的原始阶段适用时段并不相同。

en: Southern Qi is distinct from Northern Qi and the earlier Warring States Qi.
The dynasty is part of an overlapping southern and northern chronology.
zh: 南齐与北齐、战国齐国不同。
它属于南北同时并立的历史，而非单线接替。

title.en: Liang: a southern court and Buddhist patronage
title.zh: 梁：南方朝廷与佛教赞助

location.label: Jiankang, present-day Nanjing; representative court location

summary.en:
The Liang dynasty continued the southern court sequence at Jiankang. Emperor Wu’s court supported scholarship, artists and Buddhist activity. The museum chronology records his Buddhist commitments and a mission to India for texts, placing the court within networks wider than the area it governed.

At the same time, northern politics changed from Northern Wei into competing eastern and western successor regimes. Liang therefore cannot stand for a single government across China. Compare the court’s religious and literary activity with northern Buddhist landscapes rather than treating the south as disconnected. The end of the dynasty also precedes the conquest of Chen: the beginning of Sui in 581 and southern reunification in 589 are separate milestones.
summary.zh:
梁延续以建康为中心的南方朝廷序列。梁武帝朝廷支持学术、艺术与佛教活动；博物馆年表还记载其佛教信仰以及赴印度求取经籍的活动，使南方朝廷置于超越辖境的联系网络中。

与此同时，北方从北魏转入东西两个继承体系，梁不能代表全中国的统一政府。可以把南方朝廷的宗教、文学活动与北方佛教景观并读，而非把南方视为隔绝世界。梁结束后还有陈；581年隋建立与589年征服陈，也是不同的历史节点。

dateNote.en: 502–557 is the museum dynastic span. The representative pin marks Jiankang; changing control during political turmoil is not reconstructed annually. Sui’s founding in 581 is not the date it conquered Chen.
dateNote.zh: 502—557年为博物馆采用的王朝时段。建康只是代表点，本条不逐年重建战乱中的地方控制。581年隋建国不等于隋征服陈的时间。

en: Liang and northern successor courts existed at the same time.
Buddhist textual exchange connected the court with South Asia.
zh: 梁与北方多个继承政权同时存在。
佛教经籍交流把朝廷与南亚联系起来。

title.en: Chen: the southern court before Sui reunification
title.zh: 陈：隋统一之前的南方朝廷

summary.en:
Chen was the last of the southern dynasties before Sui reunification. It followed Liang and coexisted with the northern transition from Northern Zhou to Sui. A timeline that replaces all southern history with “Sui” from 581 hides those final years of political separation. Chen’s bar continues until 589, the date the cited chronology uses for Sui unification.

This overlap is a useful way to read any imperial history: distinguish a dynasty’s establishment from its expansion and from the fall of another court. The map should likewise identify the stage it depicts. Jiankang locates the southern court; it does not imply a fixed frontier throughout the dynasty’s existence.
summary.zh:
陈是隋统一之前最后一个南方王朝。它继承梁，并经历北方从北周到隋的更替。如果时间线从581年起就以“隋”覆盖整个中国，便会抹去南北仍然并立的最后数年。陈应延续显示到589年，即引用年表所列隋统一的年份。

这组重叠也提供通用的读史方法：区分王朝建立、疆域扩展与另一朝廷覆亡。地图同样需要交代呈现的是哪个阶段。建康点位用于定位南方朝廷，不表示整个王朝时期都有不变边界。

dateNote.en: 557–589 follows the museum chronology for Chen in South China. Annual endpoint overlap is intentional; the atlas does not resolve the exact date within a transition year.
dateNote.zh: 557—589年采用博物馆所列南朝陈时段。更替年份可在年度尺度重叠，本图集不据此判断同年内的精确交接日。

en: Chen continued for years after Sui was established in the north.
589 and 581 answer different questions about the rise of Sui.
zh: 隋在北方建立后，陈仍延续数年。
589年与581年分别对应隋统一与建国。

title.en: Liao: a Khitan empire alongside the Song
title.zh: 辽：与宋并立的契丹帝国

location.label: Liao Shangjing region; representative early capital reference

summary.en:
The Khitan-led Liao ruled to the north of the Song and must appear as a contemporary polity, not an empty margin around the Song map. The Shanyuan settlement established a diplomatic relationship involving boundaries and annual payments. Interaction also extended through writing, craftsmanship, agriculture and courtly material culture.

Liao tombs and objects preserve evidence that political frontiers did not create sealed cultural worlds. Princeton’s collection includes painted tomb and coffin panels showing courtly activities and everyday objects. The dynastic chronology also intersects the rise of the Jurchen Jin, whose defeat of Liao did not create a lasting Song monopoly in the north. Compare all three states before following the Song court south.
summary.zh:
契丹建立的辽位于宋以北，必须作为同时期政权出现，而不是宋朝地图周围的空白。澶渊之盟形成涉及边界与岁币的外交关系；双方的联系还见于文字、工艺、农业与宫廷物质文化。

辽墓和器物显示，政治边界并没有形成封闭的文化世界。普林斯顿收藏的墓葬、棺板绘画中，保留宴饮与日用器物等场景。辽的历史又与女真金的兴起相交：辽被击败后，北方也没有成为宋独占的空间。可以先比较辽、宋、金，再追踪宋廷南迁。

dateNote.en: 907–1125 follows the cited museum convention for Liao. Histories also use 916 for the assumption of the imperial title; this entry keeps the broader dynasty convention explicit. The pin is an early-capital reference, not every Liao capital.
dateNote.zh: 907—1125年采用所引博物馆的辽纪年；历史叙述也以916年称帝为重要起点。本条明确采用较宽的王朝口径。点位为早期上京区域，不代表辽的全部都城。

en: Liao and Northern Song have overlapping timelines.
Dynasty dating can differ from the date an imperial title was adopted.
zh: 辽与北宋的时间线重叠。
王朝纪年与称帝年份可能采用不同口径。

title.en: Jurchen Jin: a northern empire and the Song divide
title.zh: 金：北方帝国与宋金对峙

location.label: Zhongdu, present-day Beijing; representative later capital reference

summary.en:
The Jurchen Jin rose while Liao and Northern Song still existed. It overthrew Liao, then conquered the Northern Song capital region; the Song court continued in the south. These events formed a world of competing governments rather than a simple handover of one unchanged country. The Jin dynastic span therefore begins before the Southern Song.

Northern cultural production continued under Jurchen rule, including painting, literature and ceramics. Peace agreements did not eliminate political rivalry, and Mongol expansion eventually ended Jin. The shared timeline should show Jin, Southern Song and Western Xia together. Distinguish this Jin from the earlier Western and Eastern Jin: the similar English spelling conceals different Chinese characters, ruling houses and historical settings.
summary.zh:
女真金兴起时，辽与北宋仍然存在。金先灭辽，继而攻占北宋都城所在地区，而宋廷在南方延续。这些变化形成多个政府竞争的局面，并非一个疆域始终相同国家的简单交接。因此，金的起始年份早于南宋。

女真统治下的北方仍有绘画、文学与陶瓷生产。和约没有消除政治竞争，蒙古扩张最终终结金。共有时间线应同时显示金、南宋与西夏。英文同为Jin的金朝和早先西晋、东晋也必须区分：汉字、统治家族与时代环境均不同。

dateNote.en: 1115–1234 is the Jin dynastic span in the museum chronology. It is not the interval of control at Beijing, which the representative pin uses for orientation. “Jurchen Jin” distinguishes 金 from earlier 晋.
dateNote.zh: 1115—1234年为博物馆采用的金王朝时段，并非整个时期均以北京为都。北京仅作为较晚都城的地理参照。“女真金”用于区别早先的“晋”。

en: 金 and 晋 are different dynasties despite sharing “Jin” in English.
Jin and Southern Song existed concurrently.
zh: 金与晋是不同王朝，英文拼写相同。
金与南宋同时存在。

title.en: Western Xia: a Tangut state on connected frontiers
title.zh: 西夏：交通交汇处的党项政权

location.label: Xingqing, present-day Yinchuan; representative capital region

summary.en:
Western Xia was a Tangut state in the northwest, contemporary with Song, Liao and later Jin. Its position along Silk Road networks connected political rule, Buddhist institutions and movement across regions. It belongs on the shared timeline as a polity in its own right.

The imperial necropolis near the Helan Mountains offers evidence of this world through tombs, associated buildings and flood-control works. UNESCO describes a civilization drawing on Chinese imperial forms with Buddhism at its center. Such material demonstrates institutional and religious connections without reducing Western Xia to a copy of its neighbors. The state ended under Mongol conquest in 1227; that political endpoint does not mean every Tangut cultural practice vanished at once.
summary.zh:
西夏是西北地区的党项政权，与宋、辽以及后来的金同时存在。丝路交通把政治统治、佛教机构与跨区域流动联系起来。共有时间线应把它作为独立条目呈现。

贺兰山附近的帝陵、相关建筑与防洪工程，为理解这一世界提供实物。联合国教科文组织描述其文明借鉴中原帝制形式，并以佛教为核心。这些联系不能把西夏简化为邻国的复制品。1227年蒙古征服终结其政权，但不意味着党项文化实践在同一时刻全部消失。

dateNote.en: 1038–1227 follows UNESCO’s English entry and the 2025 ICOMOS evaluation. UNESCO’s Chinese synopsis says 1032, an internal inconsistency; it is disclosed rather than silently harmonized. Dates describe the dynasty, not the full date range of every tomb.
dateNote.zh: 1038—1227年采用联合国教科文组织英文条目及2025年ICOMOS评估。其中文简介写1032年，存在内部不一致，本条明确披露。年份指王朝时段，不是每座墓的使用年代。

en: Western Xia overlapped both Song phases and the rise of Jin.
The tombs and flood-control works provide different kinds of evidence.
zh: 西夏与两宋及金的兴起存在时间重叠。
陵墓与防洪工程提供不同类型的历史证据。

title.en: Wu Zhou: Wu Zetian’s interruption of Tang rule
title.zh: 武周：武则天与唐统的中断

summary.en:
Wu Zetian founded her own Zhou dynasty after exercising power during the reigns of Tang emperors. Her reign as emperor from 690 to 705 interrupts the usual Tang 618–907 bar. A readable dynasty timeline can preserve Tang as a broader historical frame while making this change of ruling house visible.

The episode also connects political authority with textual memory. The Chinese University of Hong Kong notes that her collected works no longer survive as a complete collection, while poems and essays remain in later Tang anthologies. That distinction matters: the survival of later compilations is different from possessing an author’s original collection. This entry follows the dynasty and its evidence, not a reconstructed travel itinerary or a claim that every frontier changed in 690.
summary.zh:
武则天在唐帝在位期间掌握权力，继而建立自己的周朝。690—705年的称帝时段，构成通常“唐618—907年”这一长条中的统治家族变化。可读的朝代时间线应保留唐的大历史框架，同时让武周的中断可见。

这一事件也涉及政治权威与文本保存。香港中文大学资料指出，她的作品集《垂拱集》已佚，部分诗文仍保存在后来的唐代总集中。“后世汇编仍存”与“拥有作者原集”是不同的证据状态。本条关注王朝和史料，不重建个人旅行路线，也不主张690年所有边界随之改变。

dateNote.en: 690–705 is the Zhou reign interval cited by the Chinese University of Hong Kong. Tang remains a broader period label in the atlas; overlapping bars explain the interregnum rather than assert two uninterrupted central governments. The pin is representative.
dateNote.zh: 690—705年采用香港中文大学列出的周朝统治时段。图集中的唐仍可作为较宽历史框架；条形重叠用于解释中断，不是声称两个中央政府不间断同时统治。地图点位为代表点。

en: A broad period label can conceal a change of ruling dynasty.
Later anthologies preserve only a different textual witness from a lost original collection.
zh: 较宽的时代标签可能隐藏统治王朝的变化。
后世总集保存的文本，与已佚原集是不同的证据。
